method: Reinspected actual V1/canonical FLIP, Vermeer V2, Craft V3 scene-overview sheets and Two Goals V2 enlarged ending. Read exact current/recent master corrections and historical directions. Still samples, not continuous motion/listening or device feed proof.

works.overallImpression: Dark blue stage surrounds a pale-sky/deep-water illustration. Long vertical hull, repeated central ocean views and occasional linked detail reveals; large pale speech stays below the diagram. Geometry progresses but the overall framed field remains very consistent.

alternatives.treatment: Authentic site and monitoring images lead, with geographic and mechanism overlays.
materialChanges: Use actual credited NPS site and monitoring imagery as primary material, not original environment illustration.
Cut from observed images into a separate concise physical model.
alternatives.storyTradeoffs: Authenticity could help, but the site image centers staff/equipment rather than an unobstructed pool, and before/after images are two weeks apart with no wave motion. No authenticated July quake video inspected. Static-image zooms could repeat prior documentary weaknesses; external production assets would need exact registration and rights records.

alternatives.treatment: One abstract basin/bathtub demonstration leads before the actual geography.
materialChanges: Begin with a container moving while water rocks, rather than the remote/local event.
Reveal Devils Hole and the distant earthquake after the mechanism.
alternatives.storyTradeoffs: Intuitive forcing, but the supplied distance/place surprise arrives late and a bathtub can flatten the real-world stakes into a generic demonstration. Useful only briefly within the mechanism, not as the opening.

alternatives.treatment: Inherited FLIP-style dark water panel with a cave replacing the hull.
materialChanges: Reuse the centralized blue cutaway field and successive diagram headings.
Explain travel, waves and ecology primarily by changing labels in fixed slots.
alternatives.storyTradeoffs: Convenient implementation and broadly familiar water imagery, but geographic causality and near-surface ecology become text updates. Rejected as convenience-driven art direction; generic engineering primitives may still be reused without the inherited aesthetic.

convenienceResponse.resolution: Choose the paired geographic/local opening and evolving rocky near-surface physical scene. Reject adopting the FLIP panel grammar or documentary zooms as the easiest implementation.
convenienceResponse.chosenForStory: The audience sees what traveled and what remained local, then understands why a limited shelf disturbance matters. No forced color alternation or visual novelty quota.
